newsitem.title: USA: Jet fuel diffs weaken in U.S. Gulf in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Jet fuel diffs weaken in U.S. Gulf in thin trade.

text.p: Jet fuel differentials weakened in the U.S. Gulf in quiet dealings Friday while steady differentials in the New York Harbor were vulnerable to the downside amid ample supply, traders said.

"It's real quiet here. The expiration on NYMEX didn't help matters," said a U.S. Gulf trader, noting the expiration of the NYMEX June refined product contract clouded the base price and discouraged buyers.

Prompt airline quality 54 grade was done at 0.60 cent under the July heating oil contract, easing from a bid and ask spread of 0.40 cent to 0.15 cent under. Following the deal, traders said 54 grade was then talked between 0.50 cent and 0.25 cent under.
There was no change in the New York Harbor where 54 grade was done at 0.75 cent over the June heating oil contract, but increased supply was seen depressing values there longer term.

"We have about 2.8 million barrels more in the Harbor than we did last year and that is bound to pressure things for several weeks," said a jet fuel dealer, noting high refinery runs have contributed to the supply rise.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Wednesday that for the week ended May 23 jet kerosene stocks were 3.5 million barrels above a year ago in the whole U.S. Northeast region. The API said refinery runs stood at 96.7 percent.
Low sulphur jet was offered at 2.25 cents above the screen, a 0.50 cent rise from Thursday, but dealers said two sellers were testing an illiquid market without any buyers taking the bate.
NYMEX June heating oil ended 0.49 cent up a gallon at 56.49 cents while July heating oil ended off 0.18 cent at 55.84 cents a gallon.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
